findings.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || for team admin/owner check, requiring a user to be both admin and owner simultaneously
Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's credentials when a non-organizer adds guests
sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive the wrong email template
No server-side uniqueness validation on the guests array, allowing duplicate attendee rows to be created
Case-sensitivity in duplicate/blacklist email comparisons silently lets duplicates through because guest emails are not lowercased before comparison
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail subject indexes attendees[0] without a guard, which will crash if attendees is empty
isInvalidEmail flag is never cleared on a successful re-validation path, leaving a misleading error banner after server-side mutation errors
AddGuestsDialog empty-string initial state passes the length guard but fails validation with a misleading message

Calendar credentials are taken from the requester (ctx.user) instead of the organizer, causing non-organizer callers to fail or no-op when updating the organizer's calendar event, desynchronizing DB/emails from the actual calendar state
Authorization check for team admin/owner uses && instead of ||, so only users who are both admin and owner pass, wrongly denying team admins who are not owners
No seat-limit/capacity enforcement when adding guests, allowing callers to exceed seatsPerTimeSlot and overbook seat-limited event types

Any attendee can add an unbounded list of arbitrary email addresses with no rate limiting, max-guest cap, or organizer confirmation, enabling email/invite spam and leaking sensitive event details (videoCallData, location) to arbitrary third parties

Case-sensitive email comparison in uniqueGuests filter allows duplicate attendees (e.g. Foo@x.com vs foo@x.com) and lets mixed-case guest emails bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS; both sides should be normalized with toLowerCase()
No validation that the booking isn't cancelled or already past before mutating it, allowing guests and misleading ICS invites/emails to be added to non-active events

Unbounded `include` fetch in booking query eagerly loads `attendees`, `eventType`, `destinationCalendar`, `references`, and `user` with nested `destinationCalendar` + `credentials`, materializing a large object graph including potentially large credential JSON blobs.
N+1 translation loading: `getTranslation` is called per attendee in a `Promise.all`, likely re-reading/parsing locale files per attendee, scaling with attendee count.
Authorization runs two sequential `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner` DB queries even when team membership is irrelevant for the organizer/attendee case.

Email fan-out in `sendAddGuestsEmails` materializes promises for organizer, team members, and all existing attendees with no cap, re-emailing the entire attendee list on each add-guests action, scaling O(attendees × additions).
`replyTo` header in organizer-add-guests-email template is constructed with all attendee emails, which can grow unbounded and exceed SMTP header limits for large bookings.
`utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` invalidates the entire bookings cache rather than a scoped key, forcing refetch of all active bookings queries including large list queries.

Guest count is unbounded: schema `z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max(...)`, allowing callers to submit an unlimited number of guests, each triggering DB rows, calendar API updates, and email fan-out with no pagination or limit.
Validation in AddGuestsDialog allows empty-string entries (`[""]` initial state) to slip through, potentially passing stale empty strings in the mutate payload due to missing empty-string checks.

`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches credentials for the requesting user instead of the booking organizer, causing calendar updates to use the acting admin's credentials rather than the organizer's for team bookings.
Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both a team admin and a team owner, blocking admins who are not owners.
Server schema does not enforce email uniqueness within the `guests` array, allowing intra-array duplicates that bypass UI validation.
Raw `guests` array is passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees to incorrectly receive full booking confirmation emails.
Newly added guests receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full booking confirmation) instead of a guest-specific notification template.
Organizer email subject line uses `attendees[0].name`, which may be an empty string for new guests if Prisma ordering returns them first, resulting in a broken subject line.
`isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses AND (`&&`) instead of OR (`||`), requiring user to be both admin and owner rather than either one

`sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the unfiltered `guests` list instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` list, causing existing attendees to incorrectly receive a full scheduled email instead of the guests-added email
Email-send failure is silently swallowed with `console.log` instead of `console.error`, and the caught `err` object is not logged, making notification failures invisible to error-monitoring pipelines
Database write commits before calendar update with no transaction or rollback, leaving guests persisted in the DB even if the calendar update throws, causing an inconsistent state

`EventManager` is constructed using the requesting user's (admin/owner) credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, which may cause calendar integration to fail or write to the wrong calendar
No upper bound (`.max()`) on the guests array schema, allowing unbounded submissions that cause bulk DB inserts, email floods, and excessive calendar API calls

Error toast fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable because `message` is always a non-empty string containing at least `": "`, and `t(err.message)` may show users raw technical error keys when no translation exists
`isInvalidEmail` state is never cleared to `false` on a subsequent successful submission, causing a stale red error banner to persist in the dialog
Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the user to be both team admin and team owner rather than either, blocking legitimate users from adding guests.
Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` emails are compared as-is, allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist.
Case-sensitivity issue in existing-attendee comparison in addGuests.handler.ts, matching the same problem as the blacklist comparison.
Duplicated and divergent validation between server schema and client schema for guest emails; uniqueness check only exists client-side, allowing direct API calls to submit duplicate emails.
Duplicates within the submitted `guests` array are not filtered before `createMany`, which can lead to unique constraint errors or duplicate inserts.
`replyTo` in organizer-add-guests-email template leaks all attendee emails to every recipient, posing an information disclosure risk for bookings where attendee privacy matters.
Swallowed error in addGuests.handler.ts: caught `err` is discarded and only a non-actionable log is printed, making email delivery failures invisible and misleading users with a success toast.
Reassigning prop `value` in MultiEmail.tsx is a maintainability smell since props should be treated as read-only.
Using array index as `key` in MultiEmail.tsx while supporting arbitrary removal can cause input-state misalignment when items are deleted from the middle of the list.
Initial state `['']` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx defeats the empty-list guard (length is 1, not 0), causing confusing validation error for users who haven't typed anything yet.

Inconsistent class instance pattern in email-manager.ts: new guests receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the dedicated `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, creating a future maintenance trap where changes to the latter won't affect new guests.
Permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both an admin and an owner instead of either, incorrectly denying team admins who are not the owner.

`sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with the unfiltered `guests` list instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees whose emails were re-submitted to receive a full scheduling confirmation email and exposing an information-disclosure surface.
DB write commits before calendar sync; if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, attendees are already persisted, leaving inconsistent state without rollback or compensation.
`replyTo` on the organizer add-guests email includes every attendee's email, leaking attendee addresses to all recipients and creating a reply-storm vector.
Server schema does not enforce uniqueness of the `guests` array, only the client does, allowing duplicates to be persisted via `createMany`.
Race condition: no locking or transaction around the read-then-write of attendees, allowing concurrent mutations to pass the existing-attendee check and insert duplicate rows.
Any booking attendee (including a guest) can add further guests with no cap, no event-type opt-in, and no notification to the organizer, creating an abuse vector for invite spam.
`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` comparison is case-sensitive on input while lowercased on the allowlist side, allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist and the existing-attendee check.
`organizer-add-guests-email.ts` indexes `attendees[0]` without a guard, which will throw and fail the organizer email batch if attendees is empty.
`handleAdd` silently no-ops when the email list is emptied, providing no validation error or user feedback when the user removes every email row and clicks Add.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || for team admin/owner check, requiring a user to be both admin and owner simultaneously
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes the authorization check incorrectly uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both admin and owner rather than either one, which matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's credentials when a non-organizer adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, where `eventManager` is constructed from the *requesting* user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });`. This means if a team admin/owner or an attendee (non-organizer) adds guests, the code will attempt to update the booking's calendar attendees using that non-organizer's credentials rather than the organizer/booking owner's credentials. The diff also fetches the organizer separately (`const organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but never uses the organizer's credentials for the calendar update, reinforcing the mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive the wrong email template

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted), and only `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted via `createMany`. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to choose the template: attendees whose email is in `newGuests` get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, others get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the input `guests` includes an email that was already an attendee (thus not in `uniqueGuests` and not newly added), that attendee will incorrectly be treated as a “new guest” and receive the wrong template. The TRPC schema does not enforce uniqueness or exclusion of existing attendees, so this is a real correctness bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side uniqueness validation on the guests array, allowing duplicate attendee rows to be created
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying issue: the server does not deduplicate/validate uniqueness within the submitted guests/emails list, so repeated emails in the input can result in duplicate attendee rows being inserted (e.g., via createMany).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity in duplicate/blacklist email comparisons silently lets duplicates through because guest emails are not lowercased before comparison
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail subject indexes attendees[0] without a guard, which will crash if attendees is empty
isInvalidEmail flag is never cleared on a successful re-validation path, leaving a misleading error banner after server-side mutation errors

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is never reset to `false` in the success path (neither in `handleAdd` when validation succeeds nor in `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`). It’s only cleared on the Cancel button. Because the dialog component stays mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem`), reopening the dialog after previously entering invalid emails can show a stale error banner even after the user has corrected the emails and successfully submits. The finding’s mention of “server-side mutation errors” is not accurate (server errors only trigger a toast and do not affect `isInvalidEmail`), but the underlying stale-flag/banner issue is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog empty-string initial state passes the length guard but fails validation with a misleading message

Calendar credentials are taken from the requester (ctx.user) instead of the organizer, causing non-organizer callers to fail or no-op when updating the organizer's calendar event, desynchronizing DB/emails from the actual calendar state

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation explicitly allows non-organizer callers (team admin/owner or even an attendee: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`). But when syncing the calendar it builds `EventManager` with the requester (`...user` where `user = ctx.user`) and fetches credentials via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The organizer’s credentials are available via `booking.user.credentials` (included in the initial query) but are not used. This means a non-organizer caller will attempt to update calendars using their own credentials (likely lacking access to the organizer’s connected calendar / event reference), while the DB update and emails proceed regardless, creating a verifiable risk of calendar desynchronization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check for team admin/owner uses && instead of ||, so only users who are both admin and owner pass, wrongly denying team admins who are not owners

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that branch, despite the variable name implying admin OR owner. If the intended policy is to allow either admins or owners (common pattern), this `&&` will wrongly deny team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not considered admins by `isTeamAdmin`). This is a concrete, verifiable logic issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No seat-limit/capacity enforcement when adding guests, allowing callers to exceed seatsPerTimeSlot and overbook seat-limited event types

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), guests are appended to `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` with no check against any seat/capacity limit. Although the handler later includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` in the constructed `CalendarEvent`, those values are not used to validate whether `booking.attendees.length + uniqueGuests.length` exceeds `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`. Therefore, for seat-limited/group events where attendee count is the capacity mechanism, this endpoint can increase attendees beyond the configured limit, effectively allowing over-capacity bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any attendee can add an unbounded list of arbitrary email addresses with no rate limiting, max-guest cap, or organizer confirmation, enabling email/invite spam and leaking sensitive event details (videoCallData, location) to arbitrary third parties

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `viewer.bookings.addGuests` mutation that any authenticated user who is an attendee (`isAttendee` is true if their email is in `booking.attendees`) is allowed to call (no organizer-only restriction and no confirmation flow). The input schema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no max length, and the UI (`MultiEmail`) allows adding unlimited empty/email fields, so there is no max-guest cap enforced in this change. The handler persists the new attendees (`createMany`) and then sends emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) and updates calendar attendees (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`), where `evt` includes `location` and potentially `videoCallData`, so arbitrary third-party emails can receive event details. No rate limiting/throttling is present in the shown code. This makes email/invite spam and information leakage a verifiable risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparison in uniqueGuests filter allows duplicate attendees (e.g. Foo@x.com vs foo@x.com) and lets mixed-case guest emails bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS; both sides should be normalized with toLowerCase()

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase, but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so a mixed-case input (e.g., `Foo@x.com`) can bypass a blacklist entry like `foo@x.com`. Similarly, duplicates against existing attendees are checked with `guest === attendee.email` (case-sensitive), so an existing attendee `foo@x.com` would not block adding `Foo@x.com`, potentially creating duplicate attendees differing only by case. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation that the booking isn't cancelled or already past before mutating it, allowing guests and misleading ICS invites/emails to be added to non-active events

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), the code fetches the booking and then unconditionally updates `booking.attendees` and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no check on any booking state (e.g., cancelled flag/status) or temporal validity (e.g., `endTime` already in the past) before mutating and sending ICS/email notifications. Given `booking.startTime/endTime` are present and used to build the `CalendarEvent`, this omission can result in adding guests and sending invites/emails for cancelled or already-finished bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `include` fetch in booking query eagerly loads `attendees`, `eventType`, `destinationCalendar`, `references`, and `user` with nested `destinationCalendar` + `credentials`, materializing a large object graph including potentially large credential JSON blobs.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the Prisma query `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees: true, eventType: true, destinationCalendar: true, references: true, user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true }}}})` does eagerly load a relatively large object graph, including `user.credentials` (which can contain large/sensitive JSON blobs). That included `booking.user.credentials` data is not used anywhere in the handler (credentials are fetched later via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), so this is an unnecessary fetch and a verifiable performance/overfetch issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 translation loading: `getTranslation` is called per attendee in a `Promise.all`, likely re-reading/parsing locale files per attendee, scaling with attendee count.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code does call getTranslation() inside bookingAttendees.attendees.map(), so it will invoke getTranslation once per attendee (plus once for organizer). However, the finding’s claim that this “likely” re-reads/parses locale files per attendee and is therefore a real N+1 performance defect is not verifiable from the diff: getTranslation’s caching/implementation is not shown, and without that it’s speculative whether repeated calls are costly or problematic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization runs two sequential `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner` DB queries even when team membership is irrelevant for the organizer/attendee case.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed unconditionally via two awaited calls: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This runs both (likely DB) queries before checking `isOrganizer` (`booking.userId === user.id`) or `isAttendee` (email in `booking.attendees`). If the user is the organizer or an attendee, team membership is irrelevant to authorization, yet the code still performs these queries, making the finding a real, verifiable inefficiency introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email fan-out in `sendAddGuestsEmails` materializes promises for organizer, team members, and all existing attendees with no cap, re-emailing the entire attendee list on each add-guests action, scaling O(attendees × additions).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `sendAddGuestsEmails` which builds an `emailsToSend` array and then `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. It unconditionally enqueues emails to (1) the organizer (`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`), (2) every team member if present (loop over `calendarEvent.team.members`), and (3) *every* attendee via `...calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`, regardless of whether they are newly added or pre-existing. There is no cap/limit on attendee count or number of guests in the input schema (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`), so each add-guests action can trigger an unbounded fan-out and re-emailing of the whole attendee list, making work proportional to attendee count per addition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `replyTo` header in organizer-add-guests-email template is constructed with all attendee emails, which can grow unbounded and exceed SMTP header limits for large bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the new template sets `replyTo` to an array containing the organizer email plus **all** attendee emails: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. There is no bound, truncation, or limiting logic, so for bookings with many attendees this produces an arbitrarily large Reply-To header value, which can exceed practical SMTP/message header size limits and cause delivery/parsing issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` invalidates the entire bookings cache rather than a scoped key, forcing refetch of all active bookings queries including large list queries.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the onSuccess handler calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` with no sub-path/query specified. With tRPC’s `useUtils()`, this invalidates all cached queries under `viewer.bookings`, which can trigger refetches for any active bookings queries (e.g., list/find/get) even if only a single booking changed. This matches the finding’s claim about broad invalidation and unnecessary refetches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest count is unbounded: schema `z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max(...)`, allowing callers to submit an unlimited number of guests, each triggering DB rows, calendar API updates, and email fan-out with no pagination or limit.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (and the client-side dialog also allows repeatedly adding empty/email fields with no cap). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler uses `createMany` to insert one row per guest (`attendees.createMany`), calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` with the expanded attendee list, and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out to organizers/team members and all attendees. Because the array size is unconstrained, a caller can submit an arbitrarily large list and trigger unbounded DB writes and external side effects (calendar update + email sends), which is a verifiable resource-exhaustion/abuse risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation in AddGuestsDialog allows empty-string entries (`[""]` initial state) to slip through, potentially passing stale empty strings in the mutate payload due to missing empty-string checks.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `multiEmailValue` is initialized as `[""]`, but `handleAdd` validates with `z.array(z.string().email())`, so an empty string will fail `safeParse` and *prevent* `addGuestsMutation.mutate(...)` from being called. The server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` also requires `.email()`. So empty-string entries do not “slip through” into the mutate payload; they instead block submission (a UX issue), which differs from the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches credentials for the requesting user instead of the booking organizer, causing calendar updates to use the acting admin's credentials rather than the organizer's for team bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using an `EventManager` constructed with `credentials` fetched from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. `ctx.user` is the authenticated *requesting* user (could be a team admin/owner or an attendee per the permission checks), not necessarily the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer` fetched earlier). Since the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to perform the action, using the requester’s credentials can cause calendar updates to be attempted with the wrong account’s integrations rather than the organizer’s, which is a correctness defect directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both a team admin and a team owner, blocking admins who are not owners.

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission gate:

```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```

will therefore reject team admins who are not owners (unless they are also the organizer/attendee). That matches the finding and is a real authorization/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema does not enforce email uniqueness within the `guests` array, allowing intra-array duplicates that bypass UI validation.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the provided `guests` array itself. Therefore a client can send `guests: ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` and both entries will remain in `uniqueGuests` and be passed to `createMany`, bypassing the UI’s uniqueness refine.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw `guests` array is passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees to incorrectly receive full booking confirmation emails.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted) and only creates DB attendee records from `uniqueGuests`. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (raw input) instead of `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which email to send, so any existing attendee email present in the raw input will be treated as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full confirmation) even though they were not newly added. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by passing the wrong array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Newly added guests receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full booking confirmation) instead of a guest-specific notification template.
Organizer email subject line uses `attendees[0].name`, which may be an empty string for new guests if Prisma ordering returns them first, resulting in a broken subject line.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are created with `name: ""` (empty string) and then `attendeesList` is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees` without any explicit ordering. Since Prisma does not guarantee ordering unless specified, `attendees[0]` can be one of the newly created guests (or any attendee with an empty name), causing the organizer email subject to render with an empty `{{name}}` (e.g., "Guests Added: X with  at Y"). This is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses AND (`&&`) instead of OR (`||`), requiring user to be both admin and owner rather than either one

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which only returns true if the user is both an admin and an owner. Given the variable name (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) and the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this likely unintentionally blocks team admins (who are not owners) and team owners (if ownership doesn’t also satisfy `isTeamAdmin`) from adding guests. An `||` would match the stated intent of “admin or owner”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the unfiltered `guests` list instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` list, causing existing attendees to incorrectly receive a full scheduled email instead of the guests-added email

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by removing emails that are already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). Those are the only guests actually added to the booking. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered `guests` input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which template to send; thus any existing attendee email that was included in the request will be treated as a “new guest” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing `uniqueGuests` (or otherwise tracking the truly added emails) is necessary to avoid this incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failure is silently swallowed with `console.log` instead of `console.error`, and the caught `err` object is not logged, making notification failures invisible to error-monitoring pipelines

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` call is wrapped in a `try/catch` that does not rethrow and only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (it neither uses `console.error` nor logs the caught `err`). This means email-send failures are effectively swallowed and the actual error details are lost, which can make failures hard to detect/monitor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Database write commits before calendar update with no transaction or rollback, leaving guests persisted in the DB even if the calendar update throws, causing an inconsistent state

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. That calendar update is not wrapped in a transaction with the DB write and is not caught; if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error out while the DB changes have already been committed, leaving the booking’s attendee list updated in the DB but external calendar attendees not updated. There is no rollback/compensation logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EventManager` is constructed using the requesting user's (admin/owner) credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, which may cause calendar integration to fail or write to the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler fetches the booking (including booking.user and booking.user.credentials) and separately fetches the organizer user, but when it needs to update the calendar it does `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is the requesting session user. This means if the requester is a team admin/owner or an attendee (not the organizer), the calendar update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) will run using the requester’s calendar credentials rather than the booking organizer’s credentials, which can plausibly fail (no integration/permissions) or target the wrong connected calendar account. The organizer’s credentials are available in the queried booking but are not used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound (`.max()`) on the guests array schema, allowing unbounded submissions that cause bulk DB inserts, email floods, and excessive calendar API calls

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`, and the handler uses that array to (1) `createMany` attendee records, (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with the expanded attendee list, and (3) send emails in `sendAddGuestsEmails` by iterating attendees/team members. With no explicit upper bound in the schema or handler, an authenticated caller (organizer/attendee/admin) can submit a very large `guests` array, causing large DB inserts and potentially many outbound email/calendar operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error toast fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable because `message` is always a non-empty string containing at least `": "`, and `t(err.message)` may show users raw technical error keys when no translation exists

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds `message` as a template literal: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. Template literals always produce a (truthy) string even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (e.g. "undefined: …"), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the fallback. The second part about showing raw error keys via `t(err.message)` can happen if the key isn’t translated, but that isn’t strictly verifiable from this diff alone; the unreachable fallback is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` state is never cleared to `false` on a subsequent successful submission, causing a stale red error banner to persist in the dialog

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is only reset to `false` on the Cancel button handler. On a successful submission (`addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`), the code closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but never clears `isInvalidEmail`. Since the component remains mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and controlled via `open`), reopening the dialog after a prior validation failure will still show the red error banner even though the user is starting fresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring the user to be both team admin and team owner rather than either, blocking legitimate users from adding guests.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that branch, despite the variable name and typical permission intent being “admin OR owner”. As written, a legitimate team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not marked admin) would fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be blocked unless they are also the booking organizer or an attendee, which is a concrete behavioral bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` emails are compared as-is, allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same case-sensitivity bug: the blacklist is lowercased but guest input emails are compared without lowercasing, enabling bypass with uppercase variants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitivity issue in existing-attendee comparison in addGuests.handler.ts, matching the same problem as the blacklist comparison.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the duplicate check uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` and the blacklist check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased while `guest` is not, and attendee emails are also not normalized before comparison. This makes both checks effectively case-sensitive, so a user could add an already-existing attendee again (or bypass the blacklist) by changing email casing (e.g., `Test@Example.com` vs `test@example.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated and divergent validation between server schema and client schema for guest emails; uniqueness check only exists client-side, allowing direct API calls to submit duplicate emails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different validation schemas: the client-side `AddGuestsDialog` defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` to enforce uniqueness, but the server-side TRPC input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` is only `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not de-duplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array (e.g., `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` would remain duplicated if `a@x.com` is not already an attendee). Therefore, a direct API call can submit duplicate emails despite the UI preventing it, matching the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicates within the submitted `guests` array are not filtered before `createMany`, which can lead to unique constraint errors or duplicate inserts.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate emails within the incoming `guests` array itself (e.g., `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` would remain duplicated if not already an attendee/blacklisted). The server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` also lacks a uniqueness refinement. Those potentially duplicated entries are then passed directly into `attendees.createMany` via `guestsFullDetails`, which can cause duplicate inserts or a DB unique-constraint error if `(bookingId,email)` (or similar) is unique.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `replyTo` in organizer-add-guests-email template leaks all attendee emails to every recipient, posing an information disclosure risk for bookings where attendee privacy matters.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the NodeMailer payload sets `replyTo` to `[this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. This embeds the full attendee email list into the message headers sent to each recipient in `to` (organizer or each `teamMember`). Email headers are visible to recipients, so this can disclose all attendee emails to every organizer/team recipient, which is an information disclosure risk when attendee privacy is expected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swallowed error in addGuests.handler.ts: caught `err` is discarded and only a non-actionable log is printed, making email delivery failures invisible and misleading users with a success toast.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards `err`, without rethrowing or surfacing the failure. The handler then continues and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client mutation `onSuccess` will show a success toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) even if email sending failed. This makes email delivery failures invisible to both users and (largely) logs/monitoring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reassigning prop `value` in MultiEmail.tsx is a maintainability smell since props should be treated as read-only.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component does reassign the local variable `value` (`value = value || []`) after destructuring props. This does not mutate the caller’s props object and does not introduce a functional/correctness bug in the diff; it’s mainly a style/maintainability preference (could be avoided with a default like `const safeValue = value ?? []`). Under the given criteria, this is a nit rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Using array index as `key` in MultiEmail.tsx while supporting arbitrary removal can cause input-state misalignment when items are deleted from the middle of the list.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}> ...)` and supports deleting an arbitrary entry via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. When an item is removed from the middle, all subsequent items shift indices, so React will reuse component instances/DOM nodes for different emails because the keys are unchanged relative to position. With input components (`EmailField`) this can cause real user-visible issues such as focus/cursor/selection and any internal per-field state (validation, touched, etc.) sticking to the wrong email after deletions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Initial state `['']` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx defeats the empty-list guard (length is 1, not 0), causing confusing validation error for users who haven't typed anything yet.
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that initializing the emails/guests array as [''] (instead of []) breaks the intended empty-state/empty-list logic (length becomes 1), leading to premature or confusing validation behavior before the user enters anything. This matches the golden concern about starting with an empty array and handling empty state in the component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent class instance pattern in email-manager.ts: new guests receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the dedicated `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, creating a future maintenance trap where changes to the latter won't affect new guests.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the behavior is explicitly conditional: for each attendee, if their email is in `newGuests` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, otherwise it sends the dedicated `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. This is not an “inconsistent pattern” bug in the diff; it’s a deliberate branching choice. The finding assumes new guests must receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, but that requirement is not established by the diff, and the dedicated template is still used (for non-new guests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring a user to be both an admin and an owner instead of either, incorrectly denying team admins who are not the owner.

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, permission is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Using `&&` requires the user to be **both** a team admin and the team owner. The variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and the subsequent check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) FORBIDDEN`) indicate the intent is to allow either role. As written, a team admin who is not the owner will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be incorrectly denied unless they also happen to be the organizer/attendee. This is a concrete logic bug introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with the unfiltered `guests` list instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees whose emails were re-submitted to receive a full scheduling confirmation email and exposing an information-disclosure surface.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server correctly derives `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted). However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original unfiltered `guests` input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` determines who receives the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. Passing `guests` means any existing attendee email that was re-submitted will match and will receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` again, instead of the intended add-guests notification (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). This behavior is directly implied by the diff and would be avoided by passing `uniqueGuests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB write commits before calendar sync; if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, attendees are already persisted, leaving inconsistent state without rollback or compensation.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation first persists new attendees via `await prisma.booking.update({... data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no transaction/rollback or compensating logic. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation will error out but the DB changes have already been committed, leaving the booking attendees updated while external calendar state is not. This is directly verifiable from the ordering and lack of error handling around `updateCalendarAttendees`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `replyTo` on the organizer add-guests email includes every attendee's email, leaking attendee addresses to all recipients and creating a reply-storm vector.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the nodemailer payload sets `replyTo` to `[this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. This causes every organizer/team-member recipient (the `to` field is the organizer or each `teamMember`) to receive an email whose Reply-To header contains *all* attendee email addresses. That exposes attendee addresses to all recipients of the organizer notification and encourages reply-all behavior that can email everyone (reply-storm vector). This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema does not enforce uniqueness of the `guests` array, only the client does, allowing duplicates to be persisted via `createMany`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in `addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `uniqueGuests` computation filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself. Therefore, if the client (or any caller) submits `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` and that email is not already an attendee, both entries pass the filter and are forwarded to `attendees.createMany`, which can persist duplicates (or cause a DB constraint error if one exists, but nothing here prevents the attempt).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition: no locking or transaction around the read-then-write of attendees, allowing concurrent mutations to pass the existing-attendee check and insert duplicate rows.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` does a separate read (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true }`) to decide which emails are “unique” and then later performs a write (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}})`). There is no transaction/locking tying the check to the insert, and `createMany` is not using `skipDuplicates`. Therefore, two concurrent `addGuests` mutations for the same `bookingId` can both observe that an email is not yet an attendee and both attempt to insert it. Depending on DB constraints (not shown in the diff), this can result in duplicate attendee rows or a runtime error from a unique constraint, so the race condition described is a real issue in the introduced logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee (including a guest) can add further guests with no cap, no event-type opt-in, and no notification to the organizer, creating an abuse vector for invite spam.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly allows any attendee (`isAttendee` checks `booking.attendees` for `user.email`) to add guests, and there is no cap or event-type setting/opt-in checked in the handler. However, the diff *does* add organizer notifications: `addGuests.handler.ts` calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` always enqueues `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` (and also team member emails). Therefore the claim "no notification to the organizer" is not verifiable from the diff, making the proposed finding inaccurate as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` comparison is case-sensitive on input while lowercased on the allowlist side, allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist and the existing-attendee check.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but each incoming `guest` is compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` comes directly from `guests` (validated as email by zod but not lowercased), a case-variant like `Blocked@Example.com` will not match `blocked@example.com` in the blacklist and will bypass it. Similarly, the existing-attendee dedupe check is also case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), so case variants can bypass the “already an attendee” filter if stored emails differ only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `organizer-add-guests-email.ts` indexes `attendees[0]` without a guard, which will throw and fail the organizer email batch if attendees is empty.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject is built using `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. There is no guard ensuring `this.calEvent.attendees` is non-empty, so if it is `[]` (or undefined), this will throw at runtime (cannot read properties of undefined) and prevent the organizer email payload from being generated/sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handleAdd` silently no-ops when the email list is emptied, providing no validation error or user feedback when the user removes every email row and clicks Add.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, handleAdd() begins with `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` and does not set `isInvalidEmail` or show any toast/error. The MultiEmail component allows removing email rows via `onClickAddon` which splices the array; removing the last row makes `value` become `[]`. In that state the dialog footer still renders the Add button, so clicking Add will silently no-op with no user feedback. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.
